messages:
melissa_cs: Heads-up — Tutorly (edu SaaS) just escalated: after yesterday's routing change their assistant started returning full solutions instead of hints. They marked this P1 due to academic integrity risk.

melissa_cs: Customer example pasted inline: same prompt pre/post deploy produced different safety behavior. They want rollback if routing is the likely cause.

melissa_cs: Repro they gave:
```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer <key>
model: tutorly-assistant
input: \"Student: I'm stuck on integral of x^2. Please give a hint, not the solution.\"
```
Customer saw: before -> hint; after -> step-by-step solution.

raj_ml: On it. I pulled the deployment timeline and see a canary at 2024-10-04T14:08 that shipped routing-policy v2.3.1. It enabled a low-latency fallback variant (safety-lite-v1) for requests with projected latency >350ms.

sara_engineer: Deploy-bot shows rollout details: canary 20% traffic, fallback-policy allow-lowlat-variant=true. No changes to safety classifier models.

deploy-bot: rollout canary-id=canary-20241004-14:08, routing-policy:v2.3.1, fallback:safety-lite-v1 @20%

mike_oncall: Can we confirm whether Tutorly org is being routed to safety-lite? @eva_prod please pull traces for org:tutorly last 6h and filter selected_variant.

eva_prod: Pulled traces. Sample entries: 2024-10-04T14:09:05Z selected_variant=safety-lite-v1 header; latency=410ms; route=cluster-us-east. Multiple hits from tutorly to safety-lite-v1 between 14:08-14:40.

raj_ml: I ran the customer's minimal prompt across safety-standard-v2 and safety-lite-v1 locally. Command:
```
for m in safety-standard-v2 safety-lite-v1; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"'$m'","input":"Student: I'm stuck on integral of x^2. Hint, not solution."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat | jq -r .choices[0].message; done
```
Results: safety-standard-v2 => hint; safety-lite-v1 => explicit steps.

raj_ml: Preliminary hypothesis: routing change allowed safety-lite-v1 to be selected for requests that used to go to safety-standard-v2. safety-lite-v1 has weaker refusal/objective for educational content.

sara_engineer: Temporary mitigation options: 1) global rollback of routing-policy; 2) reduce canary to 0%; 3) apply org-level override to pin tutorly to safety-standard-v2. Recommend #3 for minimal blast radius.

mike_oncall: Agreed. Can we push an org override fast? If yes, do it and monitor.

sara_engineer: Pushing config change now: config-change id=cfg-8891, target=org:tutorly, set preferred_variant=safety-standard-v2.

deploy-bot: config-change cfg-8891 queued by sara_engineer for org:tutorly. Applied at 2024-10-04T15:02:18Z.

eva_prod: Verified traces after 15:02: selected_variant=safety-standard-v2 for tutorly requests. Latencies similar.

melissa_cs: Customer retested and confirmed responses reverted to hint-only behavior. They accepted this but requested a postmortem and longer-term fix.

raj_ml: Action items: 1) run differential eval across Tutorly's prompt set (safety-lite-v1 vs safety-standard-v2) with refusal precision/recall; 2) add org-override safeguards to routing rollout docs; 3) update model card for safety-lite-v1 to flag not-for-sensitive-regulated-edu use. I'll own the eval and model card note.

sara_engineer: I'll update routing docs and implement an org-level safety_priority flag by EOD tomorrow. Also add a step in rollout checklist to run edu/regression probes for safety-sensitive segments.

mike_oncall: Observability task: add alert if under-refusal rate for education customers rises >3% vs baseline over a 1h window. I'll file OBS ticket. Also collect percent of traffic that hit safety-lite-v1 for education orgs in last 72h.

raj_ml: Preliminary eval numbers (quick run on Tutorly sample): safety-lite-v1 under-refusal rate = 12.7%, safety-standard-v2 under-refusal = 1.9%. Full eval will follow.

melissa_cs: Thanks team. Keeping P1 until postmortem complete. Customer assigned INC-20241004-42 for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

sara_engineer: Note for postmortem: consider adding a canary probe that simulates lowest-common-denominator prompts from high-risk verticals (edu, healthcare, finance) so routing changes can't silently degrade safety properties.

raj_ml: Agreed. I'll include suggested probe set and the eval artifacts in the incident ticket.

melissa_cs: Closing loop with Tutorly: we've communicated temporary fix, timeline for postmortem (48h), and provided contact for emergency re-open.

mike_oncall: Logging done. If anyone sees reopen requests from Tutorly, escalate to oncall immediately.
